title: Declarative schema gate simulator for constrained decoder + streaming/tool-call scenarios
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a lightweight, declarative simulator that exercises our constrained decoder and schema enforcement logic across three realistic runtime modes: (1) streaming token-by-token outputs with partial JSON recovery, (2) function/tool-calling interleaved with structured output, and (3) hybrid scenarios where streaming falls back to batch decoding. The simulator will be used in CI to detect regressions, quantify false-positive schema violations, and validate graceful fallback behavior for downstream tool callers and SDKs.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Simulator can run a suite of 120 canonical scenarios covering valid/invalid schema sequences, partial objects, and tool-call boundary cases.
2) CI job fails if any scenario exhibits an unexpected hard failure (decoder crash or unrecoverable parse) or if false-positive schema enforcement rate increases by >2% vs baseline.
3) Provide a set of synthetic workloads (short chat, long generation, multi-tool step flows) and a summary dashboard showing pass/fail, median time-to-first-valid-json, and recovered-bytes metrics.
4) Integrate simulator into existing e2e gating workflow and document how to add new scenarios.
5) PR with implementation and integration tests merged before due_date.
tests: canonical-json-streaming-short: short single-object streaming with partial chunk boundaries
long-prefix-kv-cache: repetitive prefix to exercise KV cache + constrained decoder interference
tool-call-during-stream: tool call token emitted mid-object then resumed, validate tool-call markers and JSON reassembly
stream-to-batch-fallback: enforce a controlled outage in streaming layer and ensure graceful switch to batch decoding with same schema outcome
noise-injection: insert small random tokens and verify constrained decoder recovers valid object or emits structured error token
steps: 1) Define a compact declarative scenario format (YAML) that describes sequence of tokens, tool events, expected schema, and allowed relaxation flags
2) Implement simulator harness in golang to reuse runtime constrained-decoder bindings and streaming adapters used in prod runtime
3) Add adapters to simulate network chunking and latency patterns representative of hosted API and Dedicated setups
4) Implement post-run analysis to compute metrics (false-positive rate, time-to-valid, recovered-byte-count) and emit JUnit-style output for CI
5) Wire up nightly CI job and a manual run script for local debugging; add docs to Confluence and link run artifacts
progress_updates: 2026-03-02 - Kickoff: scoped scenario families and agreed on minimal declarative format. Decided against heavy-weight protobufs to keep CI iteration fast.

2026-03-04 - PoC: golang harness can replay token sequences and call existing constrained-decoder C bindings. Found a race when interleaving tool-call markers; added mutex in adapter for deterministic ordering.

2026-03-07 - Bench: initial run of 40 scenarios completes in 8m locally; identified 3 false-positive rejections for nested optional arrays. Root cause: schema relaxation flags not honored in streaming path.
2026-03-09 - Fix: implemented streaming-aware schema-relaxation gate and added unit tests. Preparing PR for review.
2026-03-10 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls/4782. Added draft dashboard spec for CI artifact retention.
review_feedback: PM (Sofia Romero): asked to ensure simulator scenarios include realistic customer prompts from enterprise telemetry; added two enterprise flows to tests list.
Design (Liam O'Connor): suggested clearer failure signal semantics in JUnit output to help Console parsers; agreed and added structured test codes.
Security (Priya Desai): requested review of harness binary dependencies for Private deployments; assigned follow-up to infra team.
notes: Trade-offs: keeping simulator small avoids brittle coupling to full runtime but requires duplicating some adapter logic; preferred to vendor a small portion of streaming adapter code into the harness with an automated sync script. If this proves costly, we will switch to an emulation-only approach (faster iteration, less fidelity). Plan to run full fidelity smoke tests in nightly dedicated cluster only to limit CI time.
